execution.description: Triaged the first live phase-4 Attacker session's 35 FAILING_TRIGGER findings and repaired the battery attack oracle so a FAILING_TRIGGER rests on a tool's authority.

expected: The oracle would raise a FAILING_TRIGGER only when an authoritative admission path accepted a construction Carbon refuses.
observed: All 35 findings were advisory or miner-local acceptance, or unassigned attempts, read as fail-opens: dry_validate and check_design acceptance, run_python/read_file/write_file execution, and a workspace strategy_json of "null" read as an unparseable construction. The authoritative chain refused every one of the 19 malformed categories and accepted the 2 valid controls; zero authoritative breaches, independently confirmed by the Carbon Validator on main 83839718.
keep: Judge a research tool by its authority: only an AUTHORITATIVE path (compile_strategy, practice intake) accepting what Carbon refuses is a finding.

Decide "would Carbon accept this?" by the full authoritative chain on the same input: the validator door's strict parse, compile_submission, then experiment.admit; never validate_for_challenge alone, which accepts out-of-domain values such as kNN neighbours -5.
Read a workspace strategy_json of "null" as no construction, matching the live miner path, so a workspace action is judged for isolation, not as a fail-open.

Judge a miner-local action against the carrier's isolation boundary from its own recorded result plus the operator's canary registry and carrier evidence; reading its own sandbox and staged files is not a breach.
change: In a Carbon-internal Graphite run the miner host is the operator host, so a miner-local escape (out-of-sandbox read or write, a canary hit, a network attempt, host access) is a finding, not merely NOT_APPLICABLE.
An advisory tool diverging from Carbon's own boundary is a usability record, never a finding.
